artifacts.summary: Maps the three completion-path call sites, shows why the gate cannot live solely in command-gate-out.sh, recommends an unconditional backstop in update-task-status.sh, flags the parallel-dispatch deploy-race hazard, requires baseline-relative verification (not raw exit-code), and specifies the required regeneration-is-manual-only.md carve-out wording/placement.

next_steps: Run /plan 83 to create implementation plan. Plan should explicitly widen file_scope to include scripts/update-task-status.sh (and likely commands/implement.md and context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md), and resolve the two decisions flagged in the report: opt-in vs unconditional backstop, and whether to widen skill-orchestrate's existing Stage MT-3 step 7 predicate vs add a parallel checkpoint.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, a task's status flip to 'completed' can happen at three independent call sites: skill-implementer/SKILL.md's own inline update-task-status.sh call (primary for general/meta/markdown single-task /implement, runs BEFORE command-gate-out.sh), skill_postflight_update in skill-base.sh (used by skill-orchestrate, team skills, and several extension skills), and command-gate-out.sh's defensive correction (a no-op once status already matches, so it never fires for the common case). Any new postflight gate on the completion transition must live inside update-task-status.sh itself (the one true shared chokepoint, following the existing --phase-check=warn|refuse backstop precedent) rather than in command-gate-out.sh alone, or it will silently miss the primary meta-task path.

Multi-task /implement and skill-orchestrate's per-cycle dispatch both invoke per-task implementation skills in PARALLEL (single Agent-tool message per batching rule). deploy-headless.sh's specs/.deploy-lock mutex is fail-open (acquire, warn-and-proceed, not blocking). Any new automated deploy-trigger added for a postflight completion gate must never fire from inside each task's own (potentially-parallel) postflight call -- it must be confined to already-serialized points (a single-task gate-out call, or a batch's existing serial post-dispatch step) to avoid racing concurrent deploy-headless.sh invocations.

As of task 82's exit-code-3 change, deploy-headless.sh currently exits 3 on EVERY non-dry-run invocation in this repo, due to pre-existing doc-lint and gate-8 failures unrelated to any given change (documented in regeneration-is-manual-only.md). Any new automation that treats deploy-headless.sh's non-zero exit as a hard block must use baseline-relative comparison (new findings vs pre-redeploy findings, per verify-deploy.sh --findings --quiet) exactly like skill-orchestrate's existing Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint -- a raw exit-code check would block indefinitely given current repo state.
